evidence: src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:56-70: when Sec-Fetch-Site is absent and Origin is the literal null, isCrossSite returns false. Captured from a throwaway vitest probe driving the real POST handler (probe/matrix.probe.test.ts, household context and uploadStatement mocked as test/app/share-route.test.ts does): 'origin=null sfs=null -> 303 upload=1'.

Origin: null with no Sec-Fetch-Site is what a POST from a sandboxed iframe, a data: document or a cross-origin-redirected form on another site carries in a browser that predates Fetch Metadata (Chrome before 76, Firefox before 90, Safari before 16.4). In that browser class the only thing keeping the victim's session off such a POST is the SameSite=lax attribute (node_modules/@supabase/ssr/dist/main/utils/constants.js:6).

R-087, the comment: src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:39-41 says the SameSite cookies normally keep a cross-site POST sessionless 'this check does not rely on that'. R-087, the work history: delivery/work-history/m3-p5.yaml:94-95 says 'the route's refusal stays its own rather than a property of a cookie attribute set elsewhere'. Both are true for every browser that sends Sec-Fetch-Site and false for one that does not: there, a null-Origin cross-site POST passes the check and SameSite is the whole defence.

No write is reachable today: every current browser sends Sec-Fetch-Site, the matrix refuses same-site and cross-site under every Origin, and a cross-site POST under SameSite=lax carries no session, so the middleware 303s it to sign-in (src/middleware.ts:39-54). What is left is a comment claiming more independence than the code has. That is why this is low.
findings.concrete-fix: Make the claim true instead of softening it: in isCrossSite (src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:56-70), treat Origin 'null' as not cross-site only when Sec-Fetch-Site is present (that is, 'none' or 'same-origin'), and refuse 'null' when Sec-Fetch-Site is absent. The phone's share (Origin null, Sec-Fetch-Site none) stays accepted, and so does the e2e client's absent-Origin, absent-Sec-Fetch-Site request. Add a unit case to test/app/share-route.test.ts: Origin 'null' with no Sec-Fetch-Site is answered 403 and uploadStatement is not called. If the owner would rather keep the code, qualify both sentences instead (route.ts:39-41 and m3-p5.yaml:94-95): 'on a browser that sends Sec-Fetch-Site; on an older one a null-Origin cross-site POST passes this check and SameSite Lax alone keeps the session off it'.

hazard-classes-addressed.probed: (1) The full Origin by Sec-Fetch-Site matrix, run against the real POST handler with a throwaway vitest probe: Origin absent, null, own, own-host-other-scheme, foreign, same-host-other-port, garbage and empty, crossed with Sec-Fetch-Site absent, none, same-origin, same-site, cross-site and two non-browser spellings. Captured: same-site and cross-site answer 403 with no upload under every Origin. A foreign, other-port, garbage or empty Origin answers 403 under every Sec-Fetch-Site. Accepted (303, one upload): Origin absent, null or own with Sec-Fetch-Site absent, none or same-origin, plus own-host-other-scheme. (2) Which accepted combination a hostile page can produce WITH the victim's session. A top-level cross-site form POST carries Origin evil and Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site, and SameSite=lax withholds the session (node_modules/@supabase/ssr/dist/main/utils/constants.js:6 sets lax explicitly, so Chrome's two-minute Lax-allowing-unsafe exemption for default cookies does not apply). The middleware then 303s it to sign-in and the route would refuse it anyway. A sandboxed iframe, a data: document or a cross-origin redirect carries Origin null and Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site, so the route refuses it, and as a cross-site subframe or top-level POST it carries no Lax cookie either. Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin are forbidden header names, so no page can forge none or same-origin, and a non-browser client that can forge them holds no victim cookie. The only accepted combination a hostile page reaches is Origin null with no Sec-Fetch-Site, in a browser predating Fetch Metadata. There SameSite still withholds the session on a cross-site POST, which is HZ2-001: a false independence claim, not a reachable write. A same-site sibling host is refused by Sec-Fetch-Site same-site in current browsers. Sec-Fetch-Site none is produced only by browser-started navigations: a share-sheet share, where the user picks Pulse and the content is then the user's own choice, which is the feature. (3) The real Android share (Origin null, Sec-Fetch-Site none, per round 1's Chromium source reading) is accepted: 303, upload called. The red witness route-red.txt shows that exact case failing at the round one route (Tests 1 failed | 12 passed (13), 'expected 403 to be 303'), and the e2e share now sends those headers (test/e2e/share-target.spec.ts:153-156), green in e2e-p5-fr1.txt lines 333 and 699. Chromium main's future shape (own Origin, same-origin) is also accepted. (4) The unauthenticated path is unchanged by the fix (git diff 98b4f0e 31fd73d touches only the matcher line in src/middleware.ts). requireHouseholdContext still runs before formData (route.ts:80-92), and the matcher still runs middleware for /import/share and /import/share/ (compiled with Next's own getMiddlewareMatchers). (5) No in-app form posts to /import/share (grep for SHARE_TARGET_PATH and /import/share over src finds only the manifest, the middleware and the ui index), so refusing same-site breaks no legitimate caller. (6) Not found, and noted for the next reviewer: the host comparison ignores scheme, which matters only to an active network attacker (pre-existing). A proxy that rewrites Host would refuse Chromium main's future own-Origin share (pre-existing; today's null-Origin share does not reach the comparison).
hazard-classes-addressed.cleared-because: No request without an authenticated household context reaches uploadStatement or reads the body: the middleware and then the route's own household boundary stop it, both before formData, both with a bodiless 303, so D-10 holds. In every browser that sends Sec-Fetch-Site, no combination a hostile page can produce is accepted by the route. In older browsers, SameSite=lax keeps the session off a cross-site POST. That second fact is why HZ2-001 is a comment-truth finding rather than a write path. The class's harm, an unauthenticated write path or a write driven by another site's page, is not reachable at this head. Nearby lows: HZ2-001, HZ2-002 and HZ-002, the size cap that is still open.
